'''Jeffrey Tullis Leek''' is an American biostatistician and [[data scientist]] working as a Vice President, Chief Data Officer, and Professor at [[Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fredhutch.org/en/news/center-news/2022/01/jeffrey-leek-vp-cdo.html|title=Dr. Jeffrey Leek named VP and Chief Data Officer|date=11 January 2022 |publisher=}}</ref><ref name=directory>{{Cite web |title=Jeff Leek, Ph.D. |url=https://www.fredhutch.org/en/faculty-lab-directory/leek-jeff.html |access-date=2023-02-19 |website=Fred Hutch |language=en}}</ref> He is an author of the Simply Statistics blog, and runs several online courses through [[Coursera]], as part of their Data Science Specialization.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.universityaffairs.ca/news/news-article/moocs-not-dead-evolving/|title=MOOCs are not dead, but evolving|author=Diane Peters|date=2018-02-22|publisher=University Affairs}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/stevensalzberg/2015/04/13/how-disruptive-are-moocs-hopkins-genomics-mooc-launches-in-june/|title=How Disruptive Are MOOCs? Hopkins Genomics MOOC Launches In June|author=Steven Salzberg|date=2015-04-13|work=Forbes}}</ref> His most popular course is The Data Scientist's Toolbox,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.coursera.org/learn/data-scientists-tools |title=Coursera - Data Scientists Toolbox|publisher=}}</ref> which he instructed along with [[Roger Peng]] and [[Brian Caffo]]. Leek is best known for his contributions to [[genomic]] data analysis and critical view of research and the accuracy of popular statistical methods.

== Education ==
Leek graduated from [[Utah State University]] in 2003 with his Bachelors of Science. Then went on to study at the [[University of Washington]] achieving a [[Master's degree]] in 2005 and completed a [[PhD]] in [[Biostatistics]] in 2007 with [[John D. Storey|John Storey]] as his doctoral advisor.<ref name=directory /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Simply Statistics: Interview with COPSS award Winner John Storey |url=https://simplystatistics.org/posts/2015-08-25-interview-with-copss-award-winner-john-storey/ |access-date=2023-02-19 |website=Simply Statistics}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Leek joined [[Johns Hopkins University]] as an assistant professor in [[Biostatistics]] in 2009, working at the [[Bloomberg School of Public Health]]. In 2014 he became an associate professor in [[Biostatistics]] and [[Oncology]].

Leek works in The Center for Computational Biology<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ccb.jhu.edu/about.shtml|title=Center for Computational Biology|publisher=Johns Hopkins University}}</ref> at Johns Hopkins University creating statistical packages<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.biostat.jhsph.edu/~jleek/software.html|title= Software developed by Jeffrey Leek |publisher=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://ccb.jhu.edu/software.shtml|title= Software developed by The Center for Computation Biology|publisher=}}</ref> for analysis of genomes.

He also co-edits a blog, Simply Statistics<ref>{{cite web|url=https://simplystatistics.org/|title=Simply Statistics|publisher=}}</ref> with Roger Peng and Rafa Irizarry, which contains a mix of articles on [[statistics]] and [[meta-research]].

Leek has conducted several talks at prestigious universities and locations such as a colloquium series at [[Harvard]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hsph.harvard.edu/biostatistics/2016/02/colloquium-seminar-jeff-leek/|title=What Can 20,000+ RNA-seq Samples Tell Us About How Much Of The Genome Is Transcribed? |date=16 February 2016 |publisher=Harvard Colloquium Seminar}}</ref> and a lecture at the [[New York Genome Center]] titled “Building a Comprehensive Resource for the Study of Human Gene Expression with Machine Learning and Data Science”<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nygenome.org/event-calendar/five-points-lecture-jeff-leek-phd/|title=Building a Comprehensive Resource for the Study of Human Gene Expression with Machine Learning and Data Science. | publisher=New York Genome Center Lecture|author=Jeff Leek}}</ref> as a part of their lecture series.

He is an expert in reproducibility, and his work and opinions have been published in notable scientific and medical journals such as ''Nature''<ref>{{cite journal|title= Statistics: P values are just the tip of the iceberg|journal=Nature|last1=Leek|first1=Jeff|last2=Peng|first2=Roger|date=2015-04-28|volume=520|issue=7549|page= 612|doi= 10.1038/520612a|pmid= 25925460|bibcode= 2015Natur.520..612L|s2cid= 4465756|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Five Ways to Fix Statistics|last1=Leek|first1=Jeff|last2=McShane|first2=Blakeley|last3=Gelman|first3=Andrew|last4=Colquhoun|first4=David|last5=Nuijten|first5=Michele|last6=Goodman|first6=Steven|journal=Nature|date=2017-11-28|volume=551|issue=7682|pages=557–559|doi=10.1038/d41586-017-07522-z|doi-access=free}}</ref> and the ''Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.'' Leek wrote a self-published book, ''The Elements of Data Analytic Style'' and is considered an expert on replication.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://leanpub.com/datastyle |title= The Elements of Data Analytic Style|date= 20 February 2014|publisher=Leanpub}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://hub.jhu.edu/2017/11/07/fixing-replication-crisis-in-science/|publisher=Hub|title=Could you repeat that? Fixing the 'replication crisis' in biomedical research has become top priority| author=Karen Nitkin|date=2017-11-07}}</ref>

He is currently Vice President and Chief Data Officer at Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center in Seattle, where he and his team are working on AI-supported cancer treatment discovery.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=directory />

==Recognition==
Leek was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amstat.org/ASA/Your-Career/Awards/ASA-Fellows-list.aspx|title=ASA Fellows list|publisher=American Statistical Association|accessdate=2020-06-01}}</ref> In 2021, Leek won the [[COPSS Presidents' Award]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-11-01 |title=Jeffrey T. Leek Wins COPSS Presidents’ Award {{!}} Amstat News |url=https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2021/11/01/jeffrey-t-leek-wins-copss-presidents-award/ |access-date=2024-01-31 |website=Amstat News |language=en-US}}</ref> He was named one of the one hundred most influential people in AI in 2025 by Time Magazine.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2025-08-28 |title=Jeff Leek - TIME100 AI 2025 {{!}} Time |url=https://time.com/collections/time100-ai-2025/7305795/jeff-leek/ |access-date=2025-08-29 |website=Time |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Selected publications ==
Leek's highly cited works include 
* "Capturing Heterogeneity in Gene Expression Studies by Surrogate Variable Analysis"<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Leek|first1=Jeff|last2=Storey|first2=John| title = Capturing Heterogeneity in Gene Expression Studies by Surrogate Variable Analysis| journal = PLOS Genetics|volume=3|issue=9|date=2007-09-28|pages=1724–35|doi=10.1371/journal.pgen.0030161|pmid=17907809|pmc=1994707|s2cid=151500|doi-access=free}}</ref>
* "Tackling the Widespread and Critical Impact of Batch Effects in High-Throughput Data"<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Leek|first1=Jeff|last2=Scharpf|first2=Robert|last3=Corrado Bravo|first3=Hector|last4=Simcha|first4=David|last5=Langmead|first5=Benjamin|last6=Johnson|first6=Evan|last7=Geman|first7=Donald|last8=Baggerly|first8=Keith|last9=Irizarry|first9=Rafael|url= | title = Tackling the Widespread and Critical Impact of Batch Effects in High-Throughput Data| journal = Nature Reviews Genetics|volume=11|issue=10|date=2010-10-01|pages=733–9|doi=10.1038/nrg2825|pmid=20838408|pmc=3880143}}</ref>
